title: Rapid Integrator Cost Lexicon and Messaging Notes
content:
Context and intent:
This is a working note for developer-focused messaging that ties a rapid code-first quickstart to clear, honest pricing language. Goal: create a one-page lexicon and two short scripts we can A/B test in onboarding flows and marketing microcopy. Keep it short, concrete, and engineer-friendly.

Audience framing (primary): software/ML engineers building an initial integration in <1 hour. Secondary: engineering managers evaluating cost predictability.

Key messaging pillars (engineer-first spin):
- Fast time-to-feedback: "30–60s to your first token" — emphasize local dev loop and minimal configuration (API key + single curl/SDK call).
- Measurable economics: give a small, composable unit-calculator rather than opaque per-call language (example below).
- Safe defaults for production: call out autoscaling tiers and predictable reserved capacity as separate tiers — put that behind an "opt-in" step, not the default quickstart.
- Transparent fallbacks: show how we automatically route to a cheaper compatible variant when latency SLOs allow. Engineers like control and rollback clarity.

Competitive posture (short notes):
- CloudX: sells simplicity but bundles latency and cost into opaque tiers. Hook: show token math next to demo so engineers can do the arithmetic immediately.
- ModelHub: large catalog, weaker SLOs for multi-tenant. Hook: emphasize verified perf profiles and per-route latency graphs in-console.
- EdgeServe (self-hosted vendors): strong on security but heavy ops. Hook: position Redwood as "same API, low setup" with private deployment for later.

Pricing-language lexicon (engineer-friendly experiments):
- "Token unit" framing: always show "estimated tokens per demo" with sample costs. Example microcopy: "This request ~120 tokens -> estimated cost $0.0024 (at $0.02/1k tokens)."
- "Compute vs tooling" split: clarify that inference compute (per-token) is metered separately from premium observability/retention add-ons.
- "Starter tier" promise: free credit + 7-day usage cadence for first project; after that metered usage. Keep the switch to reserved capacity visible in console and described as a commitment with cost benefits.
- FAQ micro-answers: quick lines for common concerns (latency variability, tokenization surprises, quota spikes).

Quickstart angles (two short scripts for tests):
1) "Hello World, then Cost" (best for docs/first-run screens)
- Headline: "Run a sample request in 60s — see the cost instantly."
- Steps: 1) paste API key, 2) run curl/SDK snippet, 3) inspect response + inline cost card showing token estimate and sample monthly projection for 1000 calls/day.
- Callouts: small "why this cost" link explains batching, kv-cache, and latency SLO tradeoffs.
- Experiment metric: percent of devs who open the cost card after first call.

2) "Embed & Measure" (best for analytic/embedding-first flows)
- Headline: "Index a file, query, and measure latency/cost in your region."
- Steps: upload small doc (or paste), run indexing SDK, run a query, show embedding units used + equivalent token cost.
- Callouts: show both per-query latency and per-100k-embedding unit pricing estimate.
- Experiment metric: drop-off between upload and first query.

Example microcopy snippets (short, testable):
- Buttons: "Run sample (est. $0.0002)" vs "Run sample" — test include-price-on-button vs not.
- Inline: "This response used ~120 tokens — cost ~$0.0024. Learn how batching can reduce this."
- Modal copy for reserved capacity: "Switch to Reserved: 40% lower unit price at a 3-month commit. Recommended when you exceed 200k tokens/day."

Developer FAQ (quick answers to surface):
- Q: Why does cost vary by response length?
  A: We bill per token produced + tokens in prompt. Shorter prompts + caching reduce unit cost.
- Q: How do I control latency vs cost?
  A: Use quantized model variants for lower cost, or enable Dedicated for tight latency SLOs. Console recommends profiles based on traffic patterns.
- Q: What if my usage spikes?
  A: We provide auto-burst and fallback model variants; we notify account owners for sustained spikes.

Open questions & experiments to run (internal planning):
- Should we show price on the initial CTA or only after first call? Hypothesis: visible price reduces surprised churn but may reduce click-through.
- Recommended sample sizes for projection card: 100/day, 1k/day, 10k/day. Which resonates with indie dev vs platform teams?
- Metrics: instrument "cost-card-opened", "reserve-flow-started", "first-30-day-cost".

Concrete next steps (owner + short timeline):
- Short copy variants for A/B (Aisha) — 1 week.
- UX mock: cost-card with token math (Design) — 2 weeks.
- Analytics instrumentation: add events + dimension for dev vs prod API keys (Product Ops) — 1 week.
- Run 2-week A/B in onboarding and evaluate conversion to first paid project.

Notes to self / rough lines to test in Slack/email snippets:
- "See your first response and the estimated cost in one click — no surprises, no hidden tiers."
- "From hello-world to SLA: start free, pay per token, reserve when you scale."

References and links (internal):
- Quickstart repo with sample snippets: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart-examples
- Price calculator prototype: confluence://GTM/price-calc-pt1

End of doc.

(Working doc: raw phrasing OK, save final copy once A/B results in.)
